verdict.rationale: Ubuntu Desktop is an operating system you download and install on your own hardware, so the core product runs entirely under the user's control. The docs cover downloading and installing it in place of or alongside Windows, creating a bootable USB, and installing on older PCs and Raspberry Pi. Community users report running and maintaining their own installs. Missing for 10: evidence of open-source licensing or building from source, and documentation of offline or air-gapped deployment.
